name: Quick-Dip Hydration Pulse
description: This skill ensures rapid rehydration and unblocking of stem vascular systems using a concentrated citric acid hydration pulse without damaging plant tissue. The optimal immersion duration is maintained precisely at 1.76 s (safe active window between 1.06 s and 2.0 s) before transferring stems to holding water.

learned_parameters.label: Immersion Duration
learned_parameters.rationale: Set to 1.76 s. Testing demonstrated that a duration of 1.76 s yields a perfect score of 100.0 (attempts #2, #5-#10), as does 1.058 s (attempt #4, score 100.0). Increasing duration to 2.54 s drops the score to 79.6 with feedback warning of cambium burning (attempt #3), while 4.1 s drops the score to 3.2 due to severe acid burn (attempt #1). This aligns with the Floralife Quick Dip 100 Usage Guide recommending a brief 1-2 second immersion pulse. Measured: Best sub-score 100/100 at 1.76 s. Tried 1.058 s (sub-score 100) to 4.1 s (sub-score 3). Sub-score stayed at or above 80 between 1.058 s and 2.54 s.

control_effects.effect: Controls the duration stems remain submerged in the acidic quick-dip solution. Values between 1.058 s and 1.76 s achieved maximum scores (100.0, attempts #2, #4-#10). Exceeding 2.0 s rapidly degrades the score (2.54 s scored 79.6 in attempt #3; 4.1 s scored 3.2 in attempt #1) due to citric acid burning the delicate cambium layer. Measured: Best sub-score 100/100 at 1.76 s. Tried 1.058 s (sub-score 100) to 4.1 s (sub-score 3). Sub-score stayed at or above 80 between 1.058 s and 2.54 s.

steps: Prepare a shallow container filled with undiluted quick-dip hydration solution (citric acid pulse).
Recut flower stems evenly using clean shears or a floral knife immediately prior to treatment.
Lower the cut stem bases into the quick-dip solution to a depth of roughly 1 to 2 inches.
Immerse the stem ends for exactly 1.76 s (keeping duration strictly between 1.06 s and 1.8 s).
Immediately withdraw the stems from the quick dip upon reaching 1.76 s.
Transfer the stems directly into clean holding water treated with flower food without rinsing.
caveats: Quick-dip hydration solutions have a very narrow active pulse window; leaving stems submerged longer than 2 seconds causes severe chemical burns to the cambium layer.
Do not leave stems sitting unattended in the dip container under any circumstances.
Ensure stems are placed directly into holding water immediately after the pulse to facilitate vascular uptake.
Quick-dip hydration solutions (citric acid pulse) typically prescribe very brief exposure, typically 1 to 2 seconds.

The sweet spot is centered near 1.5 - 1.8 seconds. Probing the lower boundary will delineate the full tolerance window.
Quick-dip hydration solutions (citric acid pulse) are designed for a 1-2 second active immersion pulse; exceeding 2 seconds risks cambium damage.
Quick-dip hydration solutions (citric acid pulse) require short exposure (1-2 seconds) to avoid burning stem cambium.
Quick-dip hydration solutions (citric acid pulse) require strict timing between 1 and 2 seconds to prevent burning delicate cambium tissue while ensuring uptake.
Quick-dip hydration pulses must remain within 1-2 seconds; longer exposures burn delicate cambium tissue.
